mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a 0% return under the same rate regime (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 7% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement correlates with reduced consumer confidence and investment.
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during UNRATE > 7% months.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (industrial production) exceeds 850, the next 20-day S&P 500 forward return is positive, reflecting optimism about economic strength and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: Over 60 rolling 20-day windows, the signal does not produce a statistically significant positive return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (industrial production) for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak supply growth raises recession risk.
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in 20-day windows following two consecutive INDPRO declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return is negative due to increased discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such FEDFUNDS moves.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly PAYEMS (employment) surge above 140,000 indicates labor market strength that supports equity risk appetite, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during PAYEMS expansion months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via dual demand channel reinforcement.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both proxies show simultaneous increases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where CPIAUCSL (CPI) is rising at an annualized rate above 2%, the 20-day S&P 500 forward return is negative due to inflation risk premia compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL annualized growth > 2% in the current quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative during such CPI regimes (p > 0.05).
